title: Utility Types: Type Extraction knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.
Use any whenever the types become difficult.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.explanation: Type and build features must be evaluated in the actual configured project.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Utility Types: Type Extraction”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with record and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with record and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Record”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Utility Types: Type Extraction”?
options: Assume nonnullable is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check exclude and extract, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check exclude and extract, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Exclude and Extract”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
